- RTO targets (per service tier) and how they are measured

Hi Alan — thanks for the clear list. We can provide consolidated answers and a small evidence bundle. High-level responses below (attachments included):

Attachments included: redwood_rto_rpo_summary.pdf, regional_failover_diagram.png, dr_runbook_excerpt.txt

Summary answers (hosted API):
- RTO: Critical path services (API routing, model serving) — target 60 minutes; typical recovery exercises show 45-90 minutes depending on failover scope.
- RPO: Target < 15 minutes for customer-facing state via async replication and KV cache rehydration strategies.
- Backups: Full daily snapshots of control-plane metadata and nightly datastore snapshots; incremental/transactional logs every 15 minutes; retention 30 days by default (longer retention optional). All backups encrypted at rest using customer-segregated KMS keys for Dedicated/Private customers; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS with AES-256 and TLS 1.2+ in transit.
- Regional failover: Warm-standby in a second region (primary: us-west-2, secondary: us-east-1 for most hosted customers). Automated routing with health checks; manual escalation for DNS cutover for certain leased IPs. Dedicated/Private: customers can pin regions and we provide documented failover steps in the runbook.
- DR test: last full DR exercise for hosted control plane completed 2026-07-10 (planned failover to secondary region, postmortem attached excerpt).

If you want, we can call out differences per deployment type in a table. Happy to walk through the artifacts on a short call.

Best,
